newsitem.title: UK: Celltech wins U.S. antibody patent.
newsitem.headline: Celltech wins U.S. antibody patent.

text.p: U.K. biotech specialist Celltech Group Plc said on Thursday that it had been granted a key patent covering certain forms of artificially-created human antibodies by the U.S. patent office.
Human antibodies, which are naturally-occurring proteins, are being copied for use in combatting a range of diseases, including heart disease, rheumatoid arthritis and cancer.

In a statement Celltech said the patent, which lasts until 2014, will "substantially extend" the protection of products which it is developing using antibodies, and should lead to royalties from other companies using Celltech technology.
Antibodies are being used to create a defense mechanism within the body against infections caused by organisms like bacteria and viruses.
Early antibodies derived from animals failed to work effectively because they caused a major immune response when injected into humans.
Scientists believe the ability to engineer artificial human antibodies in the laboratory, which are well tolerated by patients, has opened the way for a whole new class of drugs.
Celltech is working on antibody-based treatments for psoriasis, cancer, rheumatoid arthritis and Crohn's disease.
